probeResults.evidence: The opened plan and repository HEAD match the requested fingerprints. PIN-1–PIN-16 map to context/guardrails, Task 1, Task 2, Task 3, the mandatory Phase-2 checkpoint, Step 0, B1/B2, and authoring delivery. A1–A5 have named checks in package/invocation tests, runtime/host fixtures, profile cases, B1, and the final ledger review. End states 1–7 each have an explicit deterministic command, HARD ledger review, or named B1/B2 backstop. H1–H4 are owned initially by Task 1; H4's behavioral half continues through Task 2's actual-host diagnostic and B1. Each task has an acceptance command, while live installed observation is correctly excluded from source-test success. B1 and B2 name concrete deferral reasons, operator runners, timing, retained evidence, and cheaper local proxies. Empty task deps do not split a same-phase fact from its guard: phases are explicitly sequential, shared files have one owner at a time, and the plan records why cross-phase WAR deps are inapplicable. No default flip or new inline canonical mirror is required. Touched machine-derived documentation is covered by the bind/de-mirror/scoped-backstop rule and final ledger/receipt review. Ledger truthfulness cannot be fully decided by a deterministic command, so the final plan-faithfulness sampling is a legitimate judgment check rather than a replaceable mechanical assertion. Unread linked artifacts declared for #1848, #2097, #2235, #1880, and other issue evidence reduce independent corroboration but are explicitly recorded coverage gaps and do not contradict the plan.

probeResults.evidence: The plan fingerprint and repository HEAD matched the declared identities. Baseline inspection and a read-only gate reproduction showed that a result carrying the correct absolute path and title but deliberately false plan_sha256 and target_revision was classified on-target and produced CLEARED; changing only the title produced INCOMPLETE.

findings.claim: The migration plan requires recorded plan/repository identities but never explicitly requires each probe attestation to bind to those identities or includes a discriminating stale-same-path test, so off-target evidence can still certify the run.
findings.reality: Task 1 says to record the original plan hash and target revision and to scope target identity, while End states 2–3 require off-target results to remain visible and input identities to remain distinguishable. However, the named reusable gate currently validates only read_anchor.resolved_path and plan_title. It ignores plan content hash and repository revision. A stale or substituted plan retaining the same path/title therefore passes its on-target check. Merely recording the correct identities at run level does not prove that the probe opened them.
findings.evidence: Primary source: skills/red-team/assets/red-team-gate.mjs isOnTarget() compares normalized read_anchor.plan_title and an absolute path under repo; the scaffold FINDINGS schema requires only resolved_path and plan_title. Reproduction against the frozen baseline piped one pass result whose read_anchor used the exact plan path/title but plan_sha256=64 f characters and target_revision=40 zeroes, while the envelope carried the correct fingerprint; the gate returned verdict CLEARED, expected=1, onTarget=1. Legitimate control: replacing the title with '# Another plan' returned INCOMPLETE with onTarget=0 and offTarget=['wrong-title']. Thus the failure is specifically missing content/revision binding, not malformed coverage accounting. Practical consequence: a reviewer that opened stale same-title content or the wrong repository snapshot can yield an unqualified clean result, undermining the frozen-input comparison and evidence provenance. Minimal resolution: make Task 1 explicitly require per-result plan-hash and snapshot-revision attestations validated against the run fingerprint, and add a regression where matching path/title with either stale hash or revision is rejected while the exact identity is accepted.
findings.planRef: Context baseline limitation; Binding guardrails and End states 2–3 (lines 91–95); Task 1 identity/evidence obligations (lines 121–123); B1 frozen-input evidence requirements (line 167)
